title: Stripes or Spots? Animal Patterns for Kids with Milo
description:
Stripes or spots? Look closely with Milo the bluebird and pick your answer! Then look even closer: a tiger's skin is striped too and its stripes help it hide, a baby panda is born pink and as small as a stick of butter, and every cow's spots are like a fingerprint.
An interactive look-and-find animal lesson for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, counting, actions to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.
facts: A tiger's stripe pattern is unique like a fingerprint and is also visible on its skin; the stripes help it blend in with grasses and trees; tigers are the biggest cats and very adept swimmers with partially webbed toes, and enter water to cool off (WWF Australia, '10 facts about tigers').

A newborn giant panda is pink, hairless and about the size of a stick of butter, 1/900th the size of its mother (Smithsonian's National Zoo, 'Giant panda'); the black and white markings appear within a few weeks (National Geographic).

Giant pandas spend 10 to 16 hours a day foraging and eating bamboo (70 to 100 pounds a day), hold the stems with a 'pseudo thumb', and live in mountain forests in China (Smithsonian's National Zoo, 'Giant panda').
The black and white pattern of every Holstein cow is unique, like a fingerprint (Holstein Association USA).
Cows are ruminants: they swallow grass, bring it back up as cud and chew it again; the stomach has four chambers (Britannica, 'cud').

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are looking for patterns!
Stripes are long lines. Like the lines on a stripy sock.
Spots are round dots. Like the dots on a spotty ball.
Some animal friends wear stripes. Some wear spots.
Put on your looking eyes. Are you ready? Let's go!

segments.name: tiger
lines: Here comes an orange friend.
Stripes! Orange and black stripes. It is the tiger!
close:tiger

lines.t: Are the stripes only on the fur?

lines: No! Here is the fun fact. A tiger's skin is stripy too!
exhibit
Stripes on the fur, and the very same stripes on the skin underneath.
exhibit
And no two tigers have the same stripes.
close:tiger

lines.t: But why does a tiger wear stripes?

lines: The stripes help the tiger hide in the tall grass. Can you still see it?
exhibit
And guess what? Most cats do not like water. But tigers are great swimmers!
exhibit
Splash, splash! On a hot day, a tiger cools off in the water.
It even has a little skin between its toes, like a duck, to help it paddle!
The tiger is the biggest cat in the whole world.
A baby tiger is called a cub.
Say it with me. Tiger skin is stripy too!
close:host
Can you creep like a tiger? Creep, creep, creep. Pounce!

lines.t: Quick check! Is a tiger's skin stripy too? Yes, or no?

lines: Yes! Stripes on the fur, and stripes on the skin!
High five! You have great looking eyes.

short.title: A Tiger's Skin Is Stripy Too! Stripes or Spots?

segments.name: panda
lines: Look at this round friend, with black and white patches. It is the panda!

lines.t: Now, what color is a newborn baby panda? Black and white? Or pink?

lines: Pink! Here is the fun fact. A baby panda is born pink!
Look how tiny! A newborn panda is as small as a stick of butter.
exhibit
The black and white patches grow later, when the baby is a few weeks old.
close:cub
A grown-up panda is big. But its baby is one of the tiniest babies of all!
exhibit
The mama panda holds her tiny baby very, very gently.

lines.t: And what does a grown-up panda eat, all day long?

lines: Bamboo! A panda munches bamboo for most of the day.
exhibit
It even has a special thumb, just for holding the bamboo!
A panda eats a great big pile of bamboo, every single day!
Pandas live far away, in the cool mountain forests of China.
Say it with me. Baby pandas are born pink!
close:host
Can you munch like a panda? Munch, munch, munch!

lines.t: Quick check! What color is a newborn panda? Pink? Or green?

lines: Pink! You remembered!
What a super memory!

short.title: Baby Pandas Are Born Pink! As Small as Butter

segments.name: cow
lines: Moo! Look at this farm friend.
Spots! Big black spots. It is the cow!
close:cow

lines.t: Do any two cows have the same spots?

lines: No! Here is the fun fact. Every spotted cow has her very own spots.
Her spots are like your fingerprint. Nobody else has the same one!
exhibit
Let's count some spots. One spot, two spots, three spots!
exhibit

lines.t: And what does a cow eat all day?

lines: Grass! She munches the grass. Then she chews it all over again!
exhibit
A cow has a very big tummy, with four rooms inside, to help her eat all that grass!
Count the rooms. One, two, three, four!
And where does milk come from? From cows!
exhibit
The milk in your cup, and the cheese on your pizza, both come from cow's milk.
A baby cow is called a calf.
Say it with me. Every cow has her own spots!
close:host
Can you chew like a cow? Chew, chew, chew!

lines.t: Quick check! Do two cows ever have the same spots? Yes, or no?

lines: No! Every cow has her very own spots.
Wave bye-bye to the cow. Bye-bye, cow!

short.title: Every Cow Has Her Own Spots, Like a Fingerprint!

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We found so many patterns. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Who is born pink, and as small as a stick of butter?
Whose spots are like a fingerprint?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned so many new things today.
Stripes on the tiger. Patches on the panda. And spots on the cow!
Can you find stripes or spots at home today? Maybe on a sock. Maybe on a ball!
Thank you for looking with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
